payload.headline: Apple holds near 351.91 amid reported outages; price still above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong business whose cash flow keeps growing, but at 351.91 the price assumes faster growth than Apple is delivering, and forecasts are still being cut.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait, because the gap between support and resistance is too small to trade.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at or below 300.79; swing entry on a close above 356.09

payload.happening: Apple closed at 351.91, down 0.25% from yesterday's 352.78. That is just above a support zone at 347.89–351.46 and below a thin resistance zone at 354.13–356.09. Widespread service outages hitting iCloud, the App Store and Apple Music were reported, along with a reported growing 'China dilemma' for US tech companies. Analysts cut their estimates again: next-year earnings per share (EPS) fell to 10.6 from 10.84 a month ago, and the next report is on 2027-01-28.
payload.business: The parts of the business that show up in the numbers are healthy. Revenue over the last twelve months was 478.8B, up from 416.2B, which is growth of 15.06%. Operating margin, the share of sales kept after running costs, rose to 33.01% from 31.97%. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending, rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. The share count fell 1.56% over the year because of buybacks. Two things put this at risk. First, growth is slowing: sales in the latest quarter grew 11.72% from a year earlier, against 16.6% two quarters ago. Second, the filings show inventory up 154% while quarterly sales grew 12%. Unsold stock can force price cuts and squeeze margins. Debt (80.1B) is larger than cash (36.3B), so net cash is -23.4B, but liquidity of 56.7B is ample against cash generation of this size. Today's outage news mainly affects sentiment and reputation. A single outage does not usually change what customers buy (general knowledge). The reported China issue could touch both demand and supply, but DATA has no segment figures to size it. The latest annual report also adds a new risk about an investigation, which is a governance matter for now.

worth.text: The market pays 39.2 times trailing earnings and 33.2 times next year's estimated earnings. On sales, the multiple is 10.7, about double the peer median of 5.4. That is at the 98th percentile of Apple's own 5-year range, so the stock has rarely been this expensive. A discounted-cash-flow model (DCF) values a company by adding up its future cash and discounting it back to today. Using a 10.2% discount rate, the DCF gives 142.01 in the bear case, 196.84 in the base case and 257.51 in the bull case. Using Apple's own past price-to-sales range gives 222.27 to 300.79. The whole gap comes down to one assumption: how fast cash flow grows at the start. To justify the current price, free cash flow would need to start growing at about 27.6% a year. At 20% growth the value is 263.56. Only at 30% does it reach 385.26. Sales growth was 15% last year and 7.7% a year over three years. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 197.27. My fair-value range runs from the DCF base case of 196.84 to the top of Apple's own price-to-sales history at 300.79.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free-cash-flow growth: the price needs about 27.6% a year, while sales grew 15% last year and 7.7% a year over three years.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 136.1B from 98.8B, so the business is producing far more cash than a year ago.
Operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%, which shows pricing power is holding so far.
Analysts expect next-year revenue of 571.0B, against 478.8B over the last twelve months, and buybacks reduced the share count by 1.56%.
bear: Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales rose 12%. That points to a risk of discounting and lower margins.
Price-to-sales is 10.7 against a peer median of 5.4 and sits at the 98th percentile of Apple's own 5-year history, so there is little cushion if results disappoint.
Estimates keep falling: next-quarter EPS is down 3.8% in 30 days to 2.15, and quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.72% from 16.6%.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits above every value estimate, including 300.79, so it is too high to buy.
The top of my fair-value range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, close to the rising 200-day average of 301.66. Buying starts to make sense at or below this level.
The value if cash flow starts growing at 20%, which is still above recent sales growth. Adding is justified at this price.

longterm.why: The business is high quality and generates a lot of cash, but the price needs about 27.6% growth in free cash flow while estimates are being cut. The rule verdict reads 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price is moving sideways, just above support at 347.89–351.46 and under resistance at 354.13–356.09, which has been tested only once. That room is smaller than a typical daily move (ATR, the average daily range) of 7.87, and the macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 356.09, or after a pullback that holds the 342.73–345.08 support zone.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.6% move by 2026-12-18 and 7.7% by 2027-01-15, both before the 2027-01-28 report. That report is the next real test of inventory and growth, so there is no long-term buy above 300.79 before then.

change_mind: A close at or below 300.79 would move the long-term call from wait to buy. This is the top of the fair-value range, next to the 200-day average of 301.66.

If the 2027-01-28 report shows quarterly sales growth back above 16.6% and the next-year EPS estimate moves back above 10.84, the higher-growth valuations (263.56 at 20%, 385.26 at 30%) become more believable.
An operating margin below 31.97%, or a close below the 342.73–345.08 support zone, would point to the inventory risk turning into price cuts. That would shift the view toward avoid.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the price of 351.91 remains above the 300.79 top of every value range and the next-year EPS estimate slipped again to 10.6, while the low end of the fair-value range now uses the DCF base case of 196.84 instead of 199.9.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
